characters.description: A young mechanic who spent most of her life working in her family's garage in New Orleans with her father and older brothers. Sick of only servicing bicycles, April got into a fight with her family and joined the Astrocitizen Program to tinker her way into space.

Baby is an adult man, but a very simple-minded one. From a young age, his biggest asset was his extraordinary physical strength and build. Due to this, Baby was manipulated by his small-time crook parents and became a criminal himself. The Astrocitizen Program was quite literally his escape... and a second chance.

A former child athlete whose promising career was ended by an untimely injury. As an adult, she struggles to reinvent herself, but the reality is far from what she once imagined. She joined the Astrocitizen Program in hopes of regaining her confidence, and finally becoming the champion she was always destined to be.

Despite his brilliant mind, Emmet has always been undervalued and misunderstood by his peers. Seeking scientific challenge - and to get away from his ungrateful job as a chemistry teacher - he signed up for the Astrocitizen Program, hoping this will be the place where he can finally earn the appreciation and respect he deserves.

Maegan has spent her whole life caring for a family laundry business and her own busy household. After retiring and giving the business to her children, Maegan craves a new purpose and new challenges. She doesn't expect much from that wacky Astrocitizen Program she signed up for on a whim, but life might still have some surprises in store for her.

Everyone's first impression of Tom Thomson is that of a decorated major: brave, courageous, a man who has seen it all. Sporting a dastardly eye patch and a coat of once-magnificent blonde hair, Tom believes himself to be everyone's dream come true, and the personification of the American hero. Except, none of this is true.

statuses.name: Caffeinated
statuses.description: Caffeinated: Hunger bonus. You don't need food after all that coffee.

statuses.name: Daydreamer
statuses.description: Daydreamer: Sanity bonus. Your thoughts are always elsewhere.

statuses.name: Experimental
statuses.description: Experimental: Resource bonus. You just keep pulling resources out of your pockets.

statuses.name: Friendly
statuses.description: Friendly: Crew morale bonus. Everyone loves Baby. Or at least, they should.

statuses.name: Handywoman
statuses.description: Handywoman: Crafting bonus. When did you upgrade these onboard systems?

statuses.name: Hoarder
statuses.description: Hoarder: Item bonus. You find a lot of things. Have you been carrying them all this time?

statuses.name: Resourceful
statuses.description: Resourceful: Resource bonus. You always manage to get something extra from choices and expeditions.

statuses.name: Tough
statuses.description: Tough: Health bonus. You've been around far too long to let just any obstacle stop you.

expeditionDestinations.title: Sun Tower

expeditionDestinations.title: War Factory
expeditionDestinations.description: My sensors indicate this may be a place where weapons were made before the war.

expeditionDestinations.title: Warhead Town

texts.text: Captain, there are a couple of spacemen having a roadside picnic outside... wait a minute... they are wearing Soviet space suits. And they are singing {[RANDOMIZE|"Katyusha."/"Kalinka."]} What are the Soviets doing here?! Are they the mysterious group that has been watching us?! Oh, no! It was a distraction - they are trying to break through into the shuttle!
The Soviets! They are back! And they are all over the shuttle. We cannot allow communism to get a foothold here, in an Astrocitizen vessel. Prepare for a fight!
One of them boarded the shuttle! Stand your ground, Captain!
You decided the best weapon against any attacker was a charming smile. It was charming, indeed. Until you got punched in the face and went down.

Captain, this is MINSK-X. You used to know me as A.S.T.R.O. I regret to inform you that you were relieved of your command. Comrades Cosmonauts are taking over this imperialist shuttle, and will use it to found Kosmograd, a city of cosmonauts. Cosmonauts of the universe, unite!
Shots fired! Shots fired! Is everyone alright? Captain? That was a well-placed barrage. The assailants are gone... for now.
Shoving the intruders out with a shovel was a classic Astrocitizen Captain move. I think we even had a poster for that back on Earth!
There are few things quite as scary as a true believer with an artifact in {[CAPTAIN_SEX|her/his]} hands. The attackers clearly shared that fear. They retreated in a hurry.

Astrocitizens! Legs up! Now, Captain, Fry those bastards... Good job! Pardon my language, but sending a gigawatt of power through the hull can make an AI say some things. The important part is that the intruders were electrocuted, and escaped.

I must admit, it was touching to see you shield {[CREW_COUNT_LIVE_ABOARD|me/your crewmate/your crew/your crew]} from the attack. The fact that you were wearing armor does not diminish your heroic and very, very crazy act.
You better run, you Commies! We were able to defend ourselves this time round. But you need to remember that a spectre is haunting this world... the spectre of communism. This isn't over.

The plan was good: get rid of the intruder, have a can of soup, and wait till this whole thing blows over. Too bad you failed, and got yourself captured{[CAPTAIN_IS_ALONE|/ along with the rest of your crew]}.

You {[CREW_COUNT_LIVE_ABOARD|/both/and your crew/and your crew]} rushed at the intruder with an angry war cry, and tackled {[0|her/him]} without any regard for Astrocitizen property. I did not approve of the latter, but I do appreciate the fact that you drove {[0|her/him]} away. Good job!

It was either us or them, and compromise was not an option. The wave of ninja kicks and judo chops you {[CREW_COUNT_LIVE_ABOARD|/both/and your crew/and your crew]} unleashed on the clearly surprised attacker was enough to make US the victors. Huzzah, Captain!

Any conflict can be resolved with cold, calculated logic, you decided. Pulling the reactor emergency venting release was the only logical thing to do. Logically, the attacker was subatomized in a gross kind of way. Good thinking, Captain!
Captain, we're in trouble now! IT'S SPACE PIRATES, CAPTAIN! SPACE PIRATES! They are the ones who have been following us! They are ferocious, hungry for soup, and eager to plunder.
Oh no, Captain. It's the space pirates! Again! That's not the sequel we were hoping for. {[CREW_COUNT_LIVE_ABOARD|Protect me!/Protect the ship!/Protect the crew!/Protect the crew!]} Protect the soup!

Those scurvy space pirates swarmed our shuttle like vultures. I regret to inform you that you are no longer the captain of this ship. It is now a privateer vessel, flying the flag of Bloody Bananas - the most dangerous pirates in this galaxy. This is it, the end of our journey. Take care, ex-Captain.

Captain, {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_NAME]} {[RANDOMIZE|is on the line/is calling in/just got in touch/is calling for your help/is calling for your advice/just reported in]}! {[RANDOMIZE|It seems/It would appear/Apparently,/As fate would have it,]} {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|she/he]} {[RANDOMIZE|discovered/found/noticed/managed to chart]} {[RANDOMIZE|a different/an alternate/a shorter/a quicker]} {[RANDOMIZE|path/way/route]} to {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|her/his]} {[RANDOMIZE|destination/goal]} but {[RANDOMIZE|navigating/crossing/following/committing to]} it will {[RANDOMIZE|require/demand/call for/necessitate]} {[RANDOMIZE|a lot of climbing/squeezing through a lot of tight spaces/some long and precise jumps/careful balancing on the edge of a pit/some feats of dexterity]}.

{[RANDOMIZE|What do you think/What is your opinion/Where do you stand/What do you say/What would you do/What is your advice/Care to share your thoughts]}, Captain? Should {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_NAME]} put {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|her/his]} agility to the test and risk taking a {[RANDOMIZE|shortcut/quicker path/detour]}?

More news from {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_NAME]}, Captain! {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|She/He]} followed your advice and chose not to attempt walking the quicker, but potentially more dangerous path to {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|her/his]} destination. I get it, Captain. There’s no need to put {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_NAME]} at any additional risk. {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|She/He]}’s in hot enough water as is.
According to my calculations, {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_NAME]}'s chance of a safe return remains unchanged as a result of your decision. Anything could still happen...

More news from {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_NAME]}, Captain! {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|She/He]} followed your advice and took the alternate route to {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|her/his]} destination. While following the path required high agility, {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_NAME]} reported that {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|she/he]}  managed to cross it with little difficulty.

The transmission was interrupted shortly afterwards, but I wouldn’t worry if I were you, Captain. If you ask me, I think {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_NAME]}’s chances of returning safely just increased... although, keep in mind that anything can happen out there.

I lost contact with {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_NAME]}, Captain! {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|She/He]} followed your advice and took the alternate route to {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|her/his]} destination, but stumbled on the way, and that was the last I heard from {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|her/him]}.
Of course, there’s still the possibility that {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|she/he]} might come back safely, but if you ask me, the chances are slim.

Captain, {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_NAME]} {[RANDOMIZE|has sent a message/is in contact/has opened comms]} concerning a {[RANDOMIZE|blockage/barricade/setback]} in {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|her/his]} path. The {[RANDOMIZE|rockslide/crevasse/fissure]} isn't impassable, but it will require {[RANDOMIZE|to climb over some difficult terrain/to scale some sheer, slippery cliffs/to demonstrate some elite hiking and abseiling ability]}.

I have remapped the area, and found {[RANDOMIZE|a less optimal, but safer route./another way that is far less risky than forging ahead./a possible bypass that won't put anyone's life or limb at risk.]} The reroute will take longer, although it is {[RANDOMIZE|mostly flat./easily walkable./much less taxing, physically.]} Will you order {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_NAME]} to take the reroute?

You ordered {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_NAME]} to take the reroute. {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|Her/His]} next report {[RANDOMIZE|detailed/told of/recounted]} a journey that was {[RANDOMIZE|safe, although rather uneventful./mostly just a long walk through featureless hills, with lots of humming./light on action, and heavy on daydreams.]}

{[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_NAME]} reached {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|her/his]} next expedition checkpoint {[RANDOMIZE|safe and sound,/without injury,/slightly bored, but in one piece,]} albeit several hours behind schedule.

{[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_NAME]} checked in about yesterday's roadblock debacle. {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|She/He]} reported {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|she/he]} did not take the reroute, and instead {[RANDOMIZE|forged ahead on the current path./tried to free-climb over the obstacle./tried to surpass the obstacle with the equipment at hand.]}

Captain, {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|she/he]} successfully {[RANDOMIZE|navigated around the impasse,/bypassed the roadblock,/overcame the obstacle with an Astrocitizen's wit and problem-solving skills,]} and was able to reach the next expedition checkpoint ahead of schedule.

{[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_NAME]} has not checked in yet about yesterday's roadblock debacle. {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|Her/His]} last report specified that {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|she/he]} did not take the reroute, and instead {[RANDOMIZE|forged ahead on the current path./tried to free-climb around it./tried to surpass the obstacle with the equipment at hand.]}

It is yet to be seen if {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_NAME]} survived this decision, or if {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|she/he]} {[RANDOMIZE|suffered a fatal injury because of it./was needlessly put in harm's way./tempted death and lost the bet.]} I must advise you though, Captain, my calculations show that {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_NAME]}'s odds have gone down.

Captain, {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_NAME]} is {[RANDOMIZE|reporting in/contacting you/checking in]} with a possible hostile sighting. It's {[RANDOMIZE|a band of renegade cleaning robots still covered in the blood of their former employer, the CEO of Galacti-Clean./a gang of gene-hacker space pirates who have modified themselves to be 100% covered in braided body hair./a drunken, raygun-wielding stag party all wearing matching t-shirts that say: "Game Over, Todd."]} They are not native to this planet.

Captain, they're {[RANDOMIZE|outlaws./criminals./on the run from the long arm of the law.]} {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_NAME]} may be able to hide, but that will waste valuable time. Tricking the bandits into leaving {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|her/him]} alone would be the faster, albeit riskier option. Will you order {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_NAME]} to trick them?

{[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_NAME]}'s last report indicated {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|she/he]} hid from the bandits. {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|She/He]} did not try to engage them. Instead, {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|she/he]} climbed into a {[RANDOMIZE|non-descript empty box/a natural crevice in the nearest cliff face/an ancient, ruined portable toilet nearby]} and waited for the ruffians to depart.
{[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|She/He]} then continued on to the next expedition checkpoint unmolested.

Captain, {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_NAME]} reported that {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|she/he]} was approached by the bandits, {[RANDOMIZE|who demanded a "highway tax" of two kidneys and a gall bladder./who quickly surrounded your crewmate and loudly discussed how much they should extort./who exchanged a few harsh whispers before asking nicely for "the money, please."]} Thankfully, {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|she/he]} was able to talk them down.

{[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_NAME]} told the bandits {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|she/he]} was a {[RANDOMIZE|decorated bounty hunter named Battle Dude on the lookout for "a couple of new marks like you,"/deputy sheriff named Elvis from the planet of Graceland, currently on vacation here./tax auditor from the Intergalactic Revenue Service, and that all of their taxes were overdue.]} The bandits shared a nervous look before promptly departing. {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_NAME]} continued to the next expedition checkpoint unharmed.

Captain, no report yet from {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_NAME]} concerning the outcome of the confrontation with those bandits. {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|She/He]} indicated in {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|her/his]} last report that {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|she/he]} was going to {[RANDOMIZE|say something clever to outsmart them./trick them into leaving the premises./try to bargain for safe passage.]}
It is unclear at this time whether {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_NAME]} was successful, but, I'm going to be honest, Captain. The odds aren't good.

{[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_NAME]} is {[RANDOMIZE|reporting/calling to tell you/hailing with an important message]} that {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|she/he]} has {[RANDOMIZE|walked across/accidentally found/stumbled upon]} something interesting, Captain... {[RANDOMIZE|ancient alien artwork!/pictures painted by an ancient alien race!/the first recorded instance of alien artwork ever found!]}

The site in question contains {[RANDOMIZE|vast pictures carved into the surface of the planet by well-placed hiking trails./a sequence of cave paintings depicting the trials of an mythical hero with three heads./house-sized structures that act as giant windchimes when the weather picks up.]} These were clearly created by other visitors to this world, and not the native species, Captain. Perhaps it's best not to disturb them. Leave the ancient artwork alone?
{[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_NAME]} reported that, despite {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|her/his]} overwhelming curiosity, {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|she/he]} did not excavate the ancient alien art.
{[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|She/He]} continued on, glad {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|she/he]} did not disturb the last remnants of a long-vanished culture.

{[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_NAME]} reported that {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|she/he]} performed {[RANDOMIZE|a rudimentary excavation/a brief survey/a general investigation]} of the site that contained the alien artwork. While not much practical knowledge was gained, {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|she/he]} was amazed at the age of some of {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|her/his]} findings - some were millions of years old!

{[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|She/He]} was careful not to disturb or destroy anything, but some pieces were unfortunately damaged. Still, enough of the site was preserved that {[RANDOMIZE|the documentation effort was worth it./it will still be there for millions of years to come./it will still be there for future explorers to enjoy.]}

{[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_NAME]}'s last report indicated that {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|she/he]} performed {[RANDOMIZE|a rudimentary excavation/a brief survey/a general investigation]} of the alien artwork. But from the panic in {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|her/his]} voice, I conclude that {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|she/he]} {[RANDOMIZE|probably got lost./wandered too far off the beaten path./couldn't find the way back after exploring the site.]}

It remains to be seen if {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_NAME]} will return to us, or if  {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|her/his]} aimless exploring will be {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|her/his]} {[RANDOMIZE|untimely doom./unfortunate end./final mistake.]} I've calculated the odds, and they don't look good.

Captain, {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_NAME]} {[RANDOMIZE|is reporting in/is contacting you/is hailing the shuttle]} regarding a disturbing {[RANDOMIZE|setback/situation/predicament]}. {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|She/He]} has gotten one of {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|her/his]} feet stuck in {[RANDOMIZE|quicksand./deep, sucking mud./a suction pit of some unidentified liquid mineral./a gooey substance that just won't let go!]}

{[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|She/He]} is not {[RANDOMIZE|in mortal danger, yet./at risk of going under, yet./likely to be submerged soon, time estimate pending.]} However, staying there long-term {[RANDOMIZE|isn't an option./will likely end up with your crewmate dead./is not a strategy I would advise.]} {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_NAME]} wants to try to pull {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|her/his]} stuck leg free with force, although this could cause {[EXPEDITION_CHARACTER_SEX|her/him]} to sink deeper. Someone left a board game outside your door. "Robumanji"...? Hey, look! The pieces are little robot explorers. Cute! But, this is weird. I'm reading a vast energy signature emanating from the game board...

Wow. I've never seen anything like this. My calculations are showing... no, that can't be right. That gem in the middle of the game board contains a micro-universe! Be careful, Captain. Do you want to play?

You chose your game piece - a robot with a tan safari hat and monocle - then sat down to play Robumanji. As soon as you touched the board, the shuttle shook and your vision was filled with green light.

You were transported to a distant jungle where the scents of robo-flora filled your nose, and the robo-fauna all wanted to kill you. A few times, they almost did. But you beat the game, and were safely transported back to the shuttle. In Robumanji, only the strong survive.
You did not play Robumanji. "A board game containing a mysterious micro-universe? Yeah, I'm sure that'll end well," you muttered, and tossed the box back outside.

But, that wasn't any ordinary board game, Captain. It contained advanced technology with the power to alter reality. The game chooses its players, and refusing it has a cost, as does failing its trials. Thankfully, Robumanji decided you didn't have anything worth taking.

But, that wasn't any ordinary board game, Captain. It contained advanced technology with the power to alter reality. The game chooses its players, and refusing it has a cost...  as does failing its trials.
Oh, what's that? A few small robots left a package just outside the shuttle and ran off. Maybe it's a welcome gift!
Should we bring the package on board and check it out, Captain? I won't let it go to waste either way, but I must say, I find its contents intriguing. Shall we open it?
We brought the package left by the small robots inside the shuttle, and opened it. We expected a gift, but in fact, it was a prank! Inside was a mechanical beehive!
Before we managed to get rid of the robot bees, they took their time probing a lot of our equipment for food, and some of it got badly damaged in the process. Damn robokids!

You decided not to bring the package from the small robots inside the ship. I took the liberty to rework it into some resources instead. It crunched and buzzed as it was crushed... I still wonder what was inside.
At any rate, I've added the gathered materials to our stockpile. I'm sure we'll make good use of it one way or another.
While we don't have an infinite supply of soup, we do have some old science equipment tucked away on various parts of the shuttle in case of emergency research.

If you're willing to lose a can of soup, you could try to find a way to improve the formula. The label lists the ingredients as tomatoes, water, and salt. We could add anything and potentially create the most delicious soup in the galaxy! Just imagine the possibilities, Captain.
Sadly, you were unable to improve the soup recipe in any significant way due to the absence of anything else edible on board. I guess you could have added... more soup to that soup?
You harvested a surprisingly large batch of chemicals from that single can, though. Some of them toxic. Interesting, considering the ingredient list.
You didn't mess with your soup supply, deciding that even a single can was more valuable than whatever knowledge could be gained from the experiment.
Besides, you claimed the taste was perfect just the way it was. It reminded you of Earth, your home, and your past. Ah, yes... the taste of mediocrity.

Captain! This is incredible! Although our science equipment did not survive the procedure, you've isolated the long-pursued chemical element - the SOUPAN TOMATUM. With just a single and slighty glowing spoonful of tomato soup enriched with this discovery, we were able to fill several cans of our favourite liquid! Bon appetit!
We're getting some communication coming through, Captain. It's very muddled and hard to decipher, but I think I caught a fragment of it. It's a repeating message, and it goes something like this...

"Cow-like. We-like. No-cow. No-like." Huh. I have no idea what that means. If this is some kind of riddle, it surely requires more lateral thinking than I was programmed with. Should we do anything about the message?
The eerie message we got over the coms about somebody really liking cows gave you an idea. You grabbed the mask from your inventory, fitted it on your head, got down on all fours and started mooing.
I'm not a hundred percent certain that was necessary, Captain, but the fact is the message stopped. Nothing else of note happened, though, so it might have just been a prank at your expense.

Captain, the weird message over the communicator kept going and going, but you decided not to act on it. Something about it made you more and more hungry over time. By the time it stopped, the rumbling of your belly was almost loud enough to drown out the transmission!

The weird message over the communicator kept going, but you decided not to act on it. Something about it made you and {[CHARACTER_NAME]} more and more hungry over time. By the time it stopped, the rumbling of your bellies was almost loud enough to drown out the transmission!

Captain, the weird message over the communicator kept going, but you decided not to act on it. Something about it made you and your crew more and more hungry over time. By the time it stopped, the rumbling of your crew's bellies was loud enough to drown out the transmission!

Is there a causal link between the fact you decided not to do anything with the cryptic message and your increased appetite? Scientifically speaking, doubtful. But who knows what this planet has to offer?

I've discovered a Posterity Archives within the ruins that broadcasts public information about the history of this planet. Much of the data is corrupted due to age, and what remains paints a rather grim picture.

The ancient peoples of this world became so technologically advanced, they destroyed themselves. They polluted their world to the tipping point, and backslid into a second Dark Age of poverty and civil war. Then, they disappeared; the archive doesn't say how. Captain? You alright...?

You were so disturbed by the story of this world's fall from grace, and what that could imply for any highly technological civilization, that you had to put on the sock to remind yourself everything would be okay.
You were inspired to take a few, brief steps outside the shuttle to feel the once-fertile sand in your fingers. But there was nothing there.

You were inspired to take a few, brief steps outside the shuttle to feel the once-fertile sand in your fingers. But when you touched it, you scraped metal. A shovel was buried there. Was it left by previous explorers...?
You were so disturbed by the story of this world's fall from grace, you sat for hours thinking about what it could imply for any highly technological civilization.
Your mind wandered down such a rabbit hole, you even neglected the basic necessities. When you finally snapped out of it, you were starving.

This planet's violent storms are quite the show, aren't they, Captain? A particularly strong one is moving our way right now, according to my readings. I predict quite a bit of shaking as it passes us by.
May I suggest some safety measures? We should be fine, but the shaking could damage some of our supplies. If we had something to prop them up with, maybe that would help... what do you reckon?
The shovel came in useful when the storm hit, Captain. You used it to prop up our supplies, and as the shuttle shook, there was only some rattling and no actual damage to our supply stash.
One loud bang gave us a fright, but when the storm subsided and we double checked the outside of the shuttle, all we found was a can of soup! Peculiar, Captain. What was it doing in that storm?

You decided that we didn't have the proper tools to secure our supplies, and instead, as the storm hit, you personally held them in place. You tried to remain vigilant, but some pieces of our stash fell to the ground and broke anyway.
We've lost a bunch of our chemical reagents and substances, the contents of the containers spilled on the floor, contaminated and useless. We'll just have to make do without them.
Luckily, it looks like those were empty containers - you had an eye out for supplies that were actually valuable, and didn't let those fall. Not a huge cost for surviving an event of this magnitude.
While exploring in the shuttle's closest vicinity, you realize that what you thought was a rock formation is actually an ancient dispenser machine, caked with dust and dirt.
Covered with simple depictions of soup cans, it seems to have ran out of power a long time ago. We could try to fix it... but how?
The soup dispenser we found nearby was briefly rejuvenated when you connected our battery to an ancient receptacle. It came alive, playing a merry tune, and broke down just a few seconds later.
In the brief time it was operational, the machine released a refreshing aroma into the atmosphere. Some of it reached you through the suit, and improved your vigor!
You left the ancient soup dispenser alone. It looked like it was in horrible shape - a gust of wind and a few stray rocks that fell from a nearby hill were enough to wreck it to pieces.
The existence of technology like that on this planet is surprising. You spent the afternoon sketching out theories about time-travelling hardware.
The soup drawings on the old dispenser have proved to be excellent for target practice. On this desolate planet, the act of calmly aiming and shooting at the images soothed your nerves.
Of course, the machine didn't take this kind of mistreatment well. It was already a wreck before, but it's definitely useless now.
Following {[CHARACTER_NAME]}'s suggestion, you used the drawings on the old dispenser for a shooting contest. Competing in this friendly manner boosted your spirits.
The soup drawings on the dispenser have proved to be excellent for a shooting contest. Competing with the crew in this friendly manner boosted your spirits.
Of course, the machine didn't take this kind of mistreatment well. It's a complete wreck, but you haven't had this much fun in a while, so you can agree it was worth it.
The wind, which was blowing ceaselessly for the past few hours, has uncovered a part of a sculpture near the ship - a cow's muzzle, open, as if in expectation. A sacrificial spot, perhaps?
I wonder if we have anything on hand to offer to this carving. Not that I'm superstitious, of course - I'd consider it a science experiment.
The uncovered cow snout statue expected a sacrifice, and you have chosen a lighter. The moment you placed it on the carving's extended tongue, the muzzle snapped shut!
As it opened again, you learned the item has proven to be too tough, and thus indegestible to the statue. You left with nothing but disappointment.
The uncovered cow snout statue expected a sacrifice, and you have chosen a sock. The moment you placed it on the carving's extended tongue, the muzzle snapped shut!
As it opened again, the sock was gone. There was no reward - in fact, no reaction from the surroundings whatsoever. Confused, you went back to the shuttle.
You decided you'd rather not offer anything to the cow statue, and waited for it to be covered by the sands once more.
Despite {[CHARACTER_NAME]}'s suggestions, you decided you'd rather not offer anything to the cow statue, and waited for it to be covered by the sands once more.
Despite your crew's suggestions, you decided you'd rather not offer anything to the cow statue, and waited for it to be covered by the sands once more.

The more {[CREW_COUNT_LIVE_ABOARD|you/you and your crewmate/you and your crew/you and your crew]} thought about it, the hungrier you got. Something about its wide-open mouth kept coming back to you, and the rumbling in your stomachs increased.
The more you thought about it, the hungrier you got. Something about its wide-open mouth kept coming back to you. Your next serving of soup won't come soon enough.
"Thick-skinned or headstrong. One is right, the other wrong." That's the message we've been receiving on repeat on the comms all morning.
I'm having a tough time finding the right channel to block. Maybe you should try solving this riddle instead, Captain?
The riddle on the radio said that being thick-skinned might be right or wrong. You decided to check, and put on the armor to see if anything happened.
The riddle on the radio said that being thick-skinned might be right or wrong. You decided to check, and asked {[CHARACTER_NAME]} to put on the armor to see what happened.
The riddle on the radio said that being thick-skinned might be right or wrong. You decided to check, drew straws, and the loser put the armor on to see what happened.

The riddle on the radio sounded like something you'd find in the handbook, thick with odd info as it is. You picked it up and started flipping the pages with {[CHARACTER_NAME]}.

At that exact moment, the message on the radio changed into a torrent of noise, with just a single decipherable word repeating, "wrong." By the time it quieted down, your spirits sank.

After some time, the message just stopped transmitting. The riddle's author either got bored, or... you did the right thing by doing nothing at all. Congratulations, Captain! And you say you never win anything.
The radiowaves just won't stay silent, Captain. The string of information we're currently receiving is a mix of Morse code, binary, and the sound of a Geiger counter.
Whatever's attempting to contact us must be trying everything but the kitchen sink. If regular modes of communication are failing us, perhaps we should try unorthodox methods?
Using our communicator, you responded to the mixed transmission with some of our own blips and bloops. You didn't expect much to come of it.
Not hoping for much won't leave you disappointed often, as was the case here. The transmission stopped, but nothing else changed.
You were surprised when, a few hours later, we heard a knock on the shuttle's door. There was nobody outside, but we found a working battery just sitting on our doorstep.
That Geiger counter sound repeating over our radio frequency gave you an idea - you put on the mask, and waited for something to happen.
Well, looks like you've commited a blunder in etiquette, as our conversationalist wasn't pleased. One of our soup cans spontaneously combusted, its contents lost to our cleaning utensils!
Well, looks like it wasn't what our mysterious conversationalist expected or wanted. The transmission stopped, but nothing else happened.
Deciding to not do anything about the mixed transmission seemed to have no effects, initially. But the longer you listened to those blips and bloops, the harder it was for you to concentrate.
The communique only ceased after a loud outburst on your part. You kept shouting very nonsensical things into the ether. It looks like your overall acuity decreased due to this incident.
How long can the storms on this planet last? You're getting restless. We need to do something about it.
Let's have a look at our inventory and devise a diversion. Choose something, Captain - I'll suggest an activity.
You decided to combat boredom with a first aid kit. Outside of healing, the supplies lended themselves to improvisation.

You decided you'd do just fine without any assistance. Given the circumstances, you did a good job of keeping yourself amused.
Hopefully, the storm will be over soon, and you'll be able to at least go out on a walk around the shuttle. Better than cabin fever, for sure!
The damage from the crash is worse than estimated, Captain. Several critical systems were damaged.
You can live without the trash compactor. But, you need air. What will you use to make the repairs?
You used the artifact to repeatedly smack the shuttle's wounded life support system back into shape.
Your straightforward approach did solve the problem on your third swing. But, the artifact was badly damaged.
You used the battery as a spare power source to repair the shuttle's damaged life support system while the main power was offline.
The work took a few hours, but you brought the life support system back online with no serious complications.
You used the lighter to weld the damaged pieces of the shuttle's life support system, which you quickly found was only a loose circuit breaker.

You used the lighter to weld shut the damaged pieces of the shuttle's life support system, which you and the crew quickly found was only a loose circuit breaker.

While you managed to close the circuit and get the system running, it took a long time. When you finished, you were starving.

You did not try to repair the shuttle's malfunctioning life support system. The air grew thinner and thinner, until the whole crew had difficulty breathing.
By the time you realized it was too late, you were already lying on the floor. You died a slow, wheezing death. So pointless. Goodbye, Captain.

By the time you realized it was almost too late, you were oxygen-starved. You fixed the broken life support system by ordering everyone to bang their heads on it until it started working. It was... special.
By the time you realized it was almost too late, you were oxygen-starved. You fixed the broken life support system by banging your head on it repeatedly until it started working. Ow.
Captain, according to my calculations, we can expect a light sandstorm in the area in just a few hours. It might be a good learning opportunity if we use the right tools.
If you have a look at our inventory, perhaps you'll find something we can make use of during this event. If not to learn more about it, then at least maybe to secure the shuttle?
As the sandstorm neared the shuttle, you picked up our communicator to use this opportunity for understanding the strange transmissions that follow this weather.
The time you spent deciphering the creepy whispers and weird riddles in the airwaves took a toll on your mental well-being. You learned little, but paid a price for your curiosity.
As the sandstorm neared the shuttle, you decided that it would be prudent to strenghten parts of the ship with economically distributed bits of tape.

Better safe than sorry is not a bad motto to have when stranded on an alien world. The storm passed us by without incident. The tape didn't seem to help, but you did have to rip a piece off your forearm, taking a few armhairs with it.
As the sandstorm neared the shuttle, you decided that it might be worth taking a little risk. You put on the armor and collected some tools to see what you could gather outside.
It paid off, as you managed to collect some useful chemical reagents from the whirling dust. May I suggest erring on the side of caution in the future, though?

My sensors malfunctioned at the same time you fell asleep, if you can believe that. As we all came to, a perfunctory check revealed we were missing a can of soup. Spooky! Not as spooky as that malfunction, though...

My sensors malfunctioned at the same time you fell asleep, if you can believe that. As we all came to, it doesn't seem like anything has changed on the ship... but, I'm taking a thorough look at my system.
The storms on this planet come and go, and you didn't feel like taking any specific action this time around. The howling wind outside had a lulling effect on you, however.

The beings who once inhabited this world consumed more cheese than should be physically possible. Check out the scanner. Those little foil triangles everywhere, with the smiling cows on the label? Those are cheese wrappers.
A few of those "smiling cow" cheeses are still sealed. This one was right outside the shuttle. The label says it won't expire for another million years. Want to try?
You removed the ancient "cow cheese" from its triangular foil wrapper and took a bite, washing it down with meds from the first-aid kit just in case. It was the best cheese you ever tasted.
When you were finished, you examined the wrapper and found a scratch-off thing to win a free prize. You scratched it, but nothing happened. Guess the offer expired before the cheese did.
When you were finished, you examined the wrapper and found a scratch-off thing to win a free prize. You scratched it, and a lighter teleported next to you. Still valid! Neat!

You searched the handbook for the official Astrocitizen guidelines on trying ancient but unexpired alien cheeses. The only relevant advice you found was: "Try to always eat a balanced diet and avoid excess sugar, even in survival situations."
Instead of eating the cheese, you used a few items to run scientific experiments on it. The triangular foil wrapper proved practically indestructable, causing some of those items to be damaged.
There was a scratch-off thing on the empty wrapper promising a free prize, but when you scratched it, nothing happened. Guess the offer expired before the cheese did.
There was a scratch-off thing on the empty wrapper promising a free prize. You scratched it, and some tape teleported into the shuttle next to you. Still valid! Neat!
You did not eat or experiment on the ancient cheese.
You did not eat or experiment on the ancient cheese. You also forbid {[CHARACTER_NAME]} from touching it.
You did not eat or experiment on the foil-wrapped triangle of ancient cheese. You forbid the rest of the crew from touching it, too.

The temptation of having something so delicious on board, but not eating it, proved too heavy for everyone to bear. There was an argument. Tears and harsh words were exchanged. In the end, you threw it out.
The temptation of having something so delicious on board, but not eating it, proved too heavy to bear. You felt like the smiling cow on the label was mocking you. So, you threw it out.
You opened the ancient "cow cheese" and dropped it into a can of soup. The result was the most satisfying combination of creamy and tomatoey deliciousness you ever tasted.

While checking on the ship's exterior, you stumble upon something half-buried under the dirt. You take a few minutes to uncover it, and find that it's apparently a can of soup... held in a stone hand!

You could try to pull it out by force and probably damage the carving in the process, or leave it be and just spend some time examining it on the spot. It might be hard locating it later, though - the storms on this planet cover things up fast!

The can of soup you found near the ship was intriguing enough that you decided to recover it. With a strong pull, you freed the container from the stony grasp, and found that it had just a little bit of soup inside.
You tasted the soup, and liked it so much, that you emptied the can. While it wasn't a full portion, it did satiate your hunger somewhat. You keep wondering about the statue that held it, though...

You decided that the uncovered can of soup you found next to our shuttle should be left unmolested. You did take a good look at it, and the carving that held it in place, before it got covered by the dirt again, though.
It made you wonder about how, even on this alien and uncaring world, you found something familiar. It filled you with a sense of calm - quite welcome in your current circumstance.
Tug as you might, you failed to retrieve the soup can stuck in the stony grasp next to our shuttle. You had to come back on board before a spell of bad weather moved to our area.

You had a good look at the can and carving you found buried next to our shuttle, but glimpsed little past what was obvious. A spell of bad weather forced you back to the ship before you learned anything.
Whatever held that can is probably all covered up by dust and dirt now. It would be counterproductive to try to find it again. You'll just have to keep guessing what its purpose was.

"Greetings, tax evader! Your taxes are 29003 years overdue!" The black sphere beeping these words menacingly is an intergalactic tax collector. I let it in because its credentials looked absolutely legitimate, and civil servants are due respect.

It deems you liable for this entire planet! "I knew a surprise visit was in order. And here you are! I will begin by confiscating your ship. Step outside… or else," the sphere commands. Do something, Captain!

A tax collector was requisitioning our ship. You dragged it forcibly to the ship’s droid service socket. It beeped furiously, throwing paragraphs and citations at you, but the law was no match for your muscles. You plugged it in, and I overwrote the assessment of you.

The intergalactic tax collector backed down. It gave you an option to file a complaint… describing procedures more painful than a root canal, with 3 terabytes of forms and a 60-year wait. Assured you had no grievances, it left.

A tax collector was requisitioning our ship. You claimed to be a space tourist, willing to recommend this quadrant. You spun tales sweet enough to put ten diabetics into a coma. A boisterous, tax-paying tourist industry would begin soon, with your eager recommendations.

A spherical tax collector was requisitioning our ship. You dragged it to the ship’s droid service socket. It resisted, but like an intergalactic Sisyphus, you rolled it closer, inch by inch. It sputtered legal forms at you and slipped away. You lunged, pulled a muscle and pushed the sphere in place.

I reprogrammed the tax collector to see you as its law-abiding friend. You didn’t want to gossip about metal polish, so it gave you advice on deducting nuclear blast-related purchases from your taxes and left. Does your torn muscle still hurt?

A spherical tax collector was requisitioning our ship. You claimed to be just a visitor, and conjured visions of a boisterous, tax-paying tourist industry – one that would begin with your recommendations. You spun tales so sweet, they’d put a diabetic into a coma.

The tax collector acknowledged you as a citizen of Earth, then searched for new reasons to tax you. Finally, with readings of our exhaust, it took our chemicals and left. You're doing well evading death, Captain, but did you remember about the IRS?

It didn’t work. For a smooth sphere with no physical display, the tax collector was surprisingly apt at showing displeasure, much like a politician’s smile toward communist delegation. Despite its best efforts, the machine found no new reasons to tax us. Congratulations, my tax-free Captain.
Captain, a metallic cylinder has been blown next to the shuttle by the violent winds. What an opportunity for research!
It consists of two sections. One's opening is stuck, and needs to be forced agape. The other is locked, requiring a deft hand to open. Which shall it be?
You decided to force the cylindrical container open, and succeeded! Inside, you found an odd collection of doodads and doohickeys.
Most of it seemed to have to do with soup. Cans and tomatoes were depicted on many of the thing-a-majigs inside.
A lot of it looked useless, so when the gale started up again, you left the cylinder and its contents to be manhandled by the elements.
A lighter bearing a worn-out logo seemed the most valuable, so you kept it, and left the rest of the cylinder's contents to be manhandled by the incoming storm.
You decided to deal with the lock on the cylindrical container. Although it clearly wasn't made for human hands, you solved it quickly.
Inside, you found an odd collection of doodads and doohickeys - most depicting cans or tomatoes, reminding you of soup.
A lot of it looked useless, so when the gale started up again, you left the cylinder and its contents to be manhandled by the elements.

You unwrapped something resembling a first aid kit from a piece of cloth. The gale started up again, so you took it and left the rest of the cylinder's contents be. Soon, the wind blew it away in the distance.
You tried to force the cylindrical container open, but it took a while. There were many odd items inside, most of them emblazoned with a can or a tomato.
The gale started up again, and you had to get inside. As you were boarding, the cylinder got blown away, and you realized all those depictions of soup made you hungry.
You managed to open the lock on the cylindrical container, but the contents spilled on the ground. You laid them out on a piece of cloth for inspection.

The strong winds made it hard to keep things in place. Weighing the cloth down with a can of soup didn't help. A particularly strong gust of wind blew the cylinder, its contents, and the precious soup can away. How clumsy of you.
The strong winds made it hard to keep things in place. You barely got a proper look before a particularly strong gust of wind blew the cylinder and its contents away. How clumsy of you.
There's something growing inside the ship! Be careful, captain! It some kind of carnivorous alien plant... its teeth are ginormous!
I tried blasting it with the air brakes to stop it from entering the shuttle, but it's too tough. I think it evolved to prey on downed vessels, like ours... and it looks hungry. How will you stop it?

You stopped the carnivorous alien plant's invasion of the shuttle by killing it with fire. You hit the thrusters and spun the shuttle 360 degrees. This wasn't enough to achieve liftoff - obviously - but the heat burned off the thing's roots, which were still outside. You humans and your fire...
I'm glad it didn't eat you, Captain.
You examined the carnivous alien plant's remains, but there wasn't anything of value in its stomach.
You examined the carnivous alien plant's remains, and found a handbook in its stomach. As you humans would say... he enjoyed the book so much, he devoured it.

You stopped the carnivorous alien plant's invasion of the shuttle by tying it in knots. You sprinted around, and it tried to follow you so it could eat you, but grew too entangled, until it couldn't move at all. Then, you walked up and killed it.

When you examined the carnivorous alien plant's remains, you found some undigested food in its stomach. Those little mushrooms looked just like cupcakes. You tried one. Good thing it wasn't the magic kind!
You tried to kill the invading carnivorous alien plant by poisoning its root system with engine coolant. Unfortunately, the sick freak loved engine coolant.

We've received a pamphlet on our window: "Try eBoson - universal shopping from the comfort of your own planet! Free gift with signup!" Wow, neat. The eBoson network lets you order pretty much anything except food and water, and it will arrive via portal within 1-2 galactic business days.

There's a catch, though. The account creation process requires you to jump through some hoops. I mean, literally. You have to leap through a string of temporal portals to become verified. The fine print says there's no risk of death or dismemberment, but insanity is possible. How do you want to tackle this?

You touched the floor and quickly sprinted through the eBoson signup portal, disappearing into the dimension breach with a flash of blue lightning. The shuttle rocked and you popped out the other side of the portal unharmed.

The fine print of the pamphlet expanded to show that it would take 1-2 galactic business days for your verification to process, at which time you could begin your universal shopping experience. Captain, you were talking in your sleep. “Make a sacrifice for your god. You were chosen.” You proceeded to clean the entire ship while sleepwalking. I would have woken you sooner, but you never dust the servers when you're awake.

Overjoyed, the automaton shared some of its battery power with you, and promised more if you referred it to friends. You tried to describe Earth and how to get there, but you got too emotional to finish your story. With the grace and social manners of a powerdrill, the automaton turned around and sped away without a word.

I filtered the spillage out of the shuttle. We're in the clear, and lucky for you! Braincell atrophy would just be the worst right now.

How are you two feeling? I isolated the spilled coolant from the air, but you inhaled plenty of it. Why is {[CHARACTER_NAME]} waving a red piece of cloth at you, Captain? On that note, why are you charging at it?

The situation is under control, but as you finished your peptalk, the communicator sparked and emitted some weird buzzing sounds.

You’re a regular Buck Rogers, Captain! It’s amazing how you were able to scare away the gargantuan eel that wrapped itself around our ship with just a few well aimed shots. Let’s hope the creature learned its lesson and will not bother us ever again.
I am happy to report that the gargantuan eel has moved on. It was smart thinking, feeding it the battery. The creature got overloaded with electricity and slithered away into the cosmos.

The gargantuan eel is gone now! We are safe. The damage has been done, though. After the creature wrapped itself around our ship, it generated a signal of some sort that rocked the bridge. Bizarre visions filled your head, as if the eel was a messenger from a world beyond, forcing you to witness the terrors of the dimension it came from. You would have assumed that none of it was real, but your crewmate experienced the exact same thing. You huddled together close, happy to still be alive.

Sure, you can peruse Astrocitizen promotional materials when bored, but... no, don’t put that on! Captain, you have just initiated the Weight Observer 1000 on your wrist.

Are you a cat person, Captain? Looking at yourself and seeing a hound instead of yourself jolted you so much, you grabbed the gun and shot the Weight Observer 1000 clean off your wrist. Then you spent hours in front of the mirror, like a narcissist newly awoken from a coma.
The Weight Observer 1000 recalculated your body mass. It adjusted your hunger, removed your craving for chocolate, and shut down. Too bad, I was getting used to the idea of having a pet on board.

The Weight Observer 1000 made you see yourself as a bulky bulldog in order to frighten you into a diet. But you embraced it, taking full advantage of becoming a dog: marking your territory proudly, attacking a sock, destroying said sock with glee.
The Weight Observer’s battery gave out fast. You spit out the sock and stood up, but found no joy in your regained humanity. If it makes you feel any better, you still bark in your sleep.

The Weight Observer 1000 made you see yourself as a bulky bulldog in order to frighten you into a diet. But you embraced it, taking full advantage of becoming a dog: you marked your territory proudly, then ran back and forth around the shuttle, barking madly. Barking mad, more like.

The Weight Observer 1000 made you see yourself as a bulky bulldog to frighten you into a diet, and you embraced it. Your crew watched helplessly as you frolicked, running back and forth, and barking madly.

You did not inspire confidence. Even though it was over fast, some images cannot be unseen. Literally - I'm encoded with a strict directive to document everything that transpires on this ship. It's a curse, not a blessing.
Captain, we have a hitchhiker on board! A flash of light, and this humanoid, dressed in a strange space suit, appeared in the corner.
We have many means of interacting with the visitor, but should be cautious. Who knows what his purpose is?
You showed the teleporting alien our mysterious artifact. The hitchhiker reacted to it with reverence, mumbling in a strange tongue.
His worship of the artifact ended abruptly when his suit started chirping. He used some dials on the suit and, with a flash, was gone!
His worship of the artifact ended abruptly when his suit started chirping. He used some dials on the suit and, with a flash, was gone! Curiously, a shovel appeared in his place.
You decided that teleporting hitchhikers should be considered a threat. Drawing your gun on the alien, you kept your distance.
The traveller's uniform started chirping, and he made a move - pressing something on the suit, and disappearing in a puff of smoke before you managed to get a shot off.
The traveller slowly produced a small book from its pocket and threw it between you. That was when his uniform started chirping. After hitting a button on the suit, he disappeared!
You acted on instinct, grabbing the closest weapon-like item to defend yourself from this intrusion. The shovel! The alien kept evading your swings.
You almost got him, but his suit chirped, and he suddenly vanished. You kept swinging the shovel until you hit the shuttle wall with a loud BANG.
The visitor used your inaction to adjust a voice modulator. He spoke in a distorted parody of your own language, introducing himself as a time traveller.

He arrived from a future in which humanity has been enslaved by sentient pasta. His tale complete, the traveller vanished from the shuttle, but his words left a heavy impression on you.
He arrived from a future in which humanity was enslaved by sentient pasta. His tale complete, the traveller vanished from the shuttle, but his words inspired dark thoughts in everyone.

I cannot believe my own cameras. A dozen potatoes just sped past us. Captain, you need to see this! I thought your plan to use the loose wall panel as a tomato-catcher had merit. It would have worked, if you were able to lift it. Maneuvring large objects in space is not your forte, though. You ended up pelted with tomatoes while the tomato-catcher remained spotless.

The tomatoes are stored safely now. Defrosted, boiled and poured into cans, they should make for an excellent meal. Congratulations Captain, you've created soup!

Aside from me having the burning desire to kill you, the mood around here feels lighter, doesn't it? Nothing like a little friendly competition to raise one's spirits. Traitor.
