You didn't search the shuttle for a stowaway. The mystery child's cries haunted you less and less the farther away you flew from the nuclear war-decimated planet once known as Earth.
I doubt it was a stowaway, Captain. Nobody would stay in hiding without food for that long, even a terrified child. It was probably a stress-related auditory hallucination that seems to have passed.
Captain, I'm picking up a large object of unknown origin not far from us. It's hollow. There could be supplies inside... or maybe even other intelligent life. There's only one way to find out.
Should I activate our Super Fancy Tractor Beam? Yes, that's its official name. Charlene from Astrocitizen HQ won the naming rights at the Christmas Raffle.

You pulled the mysterious, hollow space-thing aboard and opened it. Unfortunately, the astronaut hiding inside had long since perished. Decomposition in space is interesting, Captain. I gathered many useful dat... no, you're right. I'm sorry. May he rest in peace.
You decided to let the unidentified, hollow, extremely interesting, and likely useful for data-gathering purposes, not to mention ALIEN object be. Probably the right decision, Captain!
The experience took a toll on your mental health. You kept muttering "It could have been me." I'm confused by your hypotheticals, Captain. It still could!
Both you and your crewmate suffered mentally from the experience. You kept muttering "It could have been me". I'm confused by your hypotheticals, Captain. It still could!
Everyone on board suffered mentally from the experience. You kept muttering "It could have been me". I'm confused by your hypotheticals, Captain. It still could!
Some cans are better left unopened.

There is a small creature knocking politely on the hatch. It has two heads, four arms… and soup! I’m letting it in. Let me run the translating algorithm… Captain, meet Fish. That is, Filip and Trish; They’re currently undergoing a sacred Merging Ritual that will allow them to stay together, yet literally single, forever. It prevents overcrowding, too. Look, the two chins are turning into one as we speak!

To bless the Merging with a ‘boon of abundance,’ it needs to spill soup with a stranger. Both its and theirs. You have three and a half eyes full of hope staring at you. Will you spill soup to bless them?
It was very kind of you, sacrificing soup to bless that small alien.

You decided against spilling soup. Of course, Fish started to quarrel immediately, berating itself for choosing the wrong stranger and demanding to change the name to Trip. A second later the Merging was complete and all its anger turned inwards. It departed, bitter and resentful.
But hey, it left the soup!

When you knelt gently and tipped your can towards the center of the galaxy, the alien beamed the widest smile. Then Fish repeated your moves and the Merging was complete. "Now I am truly single" it said and left, adding a little dance to its step.

Unfortunately, we have no soup. Fish didn’t take it well. It yelled at itself for picking the wrong stranger. Two of its fists clenched in anger while the other two hung motionless and depressed. It hit itself, then just shrugged. "I’m conflicted," Fish said with a small voice when the Merging was complete. "How am I supposed to live without being single-minded?" Frankly, Captain, I fail to see the problem. You live like this all the time.
Oh, gross. I thought it was just a cliché that cockroaches would be the only ones to survive a nuclear apocalypse. But it appears that a family of our hexapedal friends has hitched a ride with us.
Captain, be careful. These roaches are bigger, smarter, and far more dangerous than the average representatives of their species. You could try to kill them, or let them be. Want to go on a bug hunt?

You went on a bug hunt to kill the mutant roaches nesting on the shuttle. But they anticipated your violent approach, and you fell into their trap. They let you run around getting tired while they raided our supplies.
These were not your garden-variety roaches, Captain, but the result of some top-secret government experiment. While they didn't find anything to eat, they left you a note: "Give soup."

These were not your garden-variety roaches, Captain, but the result of some top-secret government experiment. Not only did they decimate your food stores, they even left you a note: "We eatin your soup."
You didn't hunt down the roaches, instead opting to co-exist with them aboard the shuttle. The roaches appreciated your peaceful approach, and left you something to show their gratitude.
These were not your garden-variety roaches, Captain, but the result of some top-secret government experiment. They left you a note: "Thanks for not killing us. Stay cool. Love, the Petersons."

These were not your garden-variety roaches, Captain, but the result of some top-secret government experiment. They left you a gun, along with the following note: "We can't eat this, so please take. Love, the Petersons."

Captain, I've got good news and I've got bad news. The good news is that using the airlock as a space toilet was a success! It's now packed full and ready to be emptied into space. The bad news is that the airlock hatch is jammed. If you don't fix it soon, our clogged toilet will quickly become an extinction level event.
It's now or never, Captain. How will you save the human race?
The duct tape saved the day, Captain! The airlock hatch is now fully operational and the troublesome "cargo" is gone. We are safe! I'm certain the smell will go away too. Someday.

Since you've single-handedly saved the human race, I promise I will never reveal the footage of how you managed to get to that jammed door, Captain. Unless Astrocitizen Command requests it, of course.
You and your crewmate can rest easy now, Captain. Until the next crisis, that is.
Your people are safe, Captain. What a relief for all of you.
Doing nothing about the airlock-toilet was risky, Captain. Lucky for you, the door unjammed on its own, eventually - probably because the odour build-up made it corrosive.
Too bad about all the health hazards it caused. But then again, it's a 100% human problem, which makes it 100% yours and exactly 0% mine.

Something seems to be troubling you, Captain. I've registered you keep staring outside the window, into the endless void. Why? Did you lose something? I see... you are remembering Earth. I admit, it was nice. Before the nuclear BBQ, that is.
I can switch off for a second, Captain. Do you wish to have a moment to yourself?
That's right, Captain. Keep your emotions in check and develop unhealthy coping mechanisms. That should keep you standing!

You've been worried about something, Captain, but it seems those troubles are behind you. I am not surprised by your choice to find comfort with the Astrocitizen issued Astrefact™. It is guaranteed to resolve any and all of your emotional issues.
I can't tell if it was the mumbling to or the juggling of the artifact that helped, but I am glad to see you are doing better.
Remember, you can always talk to me. When I have a good day. And when I'm not running calculations. Apart from that, anytime. Just let me know 24 hours in advance.
Why sulk by yourself, when you can share all the grim topics with your crewmate? Isn't complaining one of the human pasttimes of you humans?
You know what's better than one grim human? More grim humans!
Captain, are you all right? Those weird spots on your arms are a little worrisome. Can you see them? Please wait while I search the medical database.
SEARCHING... Unfortunately, I am unable to identify your affliction. I'm afraid you will have to diagnose it yourself. That shouldn't be too hard - doctors are overrated. Can you do that, Captain?

Weird spots appeared on your body yesterday. Luckily, you found a solution in the handbook. The spots were the first symptoms of a potentially dangerous and highly shameful ailment. At least it was easy to cure. All you needed to do was to follow the step-by-step instructions in the handbook.

Weird spots appeared on your body yesterday. You didn’t do anything about it and the situation became much worse. You tried to self-diagnose, but clearly you're not qualified enough to do that... no, Captain, for the last time, it's NOT lupus.

{[0|The affliction proved to be more dangerous than you dared imagine. Unfortunately, you are powerless against the illness. I’m afraid those are your last moments, Captain./The affliction is unlikely to develop further, but your health already took a major hit. You need to take care of yourself, Captain.]}
Attention, Captain! I am detecting a leak in our reactor coolant system! In case you were wondering - this is not good.
Did I mention you should not inhale anything that comes out of the reactor? Please, don't. Also, how are you going to fix it?

I cannot determine if you actually read the "Fix-a-reactor" Astrocitizen leaflet, or if you just made random motions trying to see anything through the mask, but the leak is no more.{[CAPTAIN_IS_ALONE|/ You will be happy to hear no one has inhaled any of the coolant vapour.]} Well done, Captain!
Not only did you fix the leak, but you also used the fumes to fuel up your old lucky lighter. Practical!

Teamwork goes so much better when a group of humans is faced with the possibility of a radioactive death. With all the chaos and cries for help, I can't even tell which one of you managed to fix the leak in the end. Too bad you inhaled quite a bit of coolant in the process.

Captain, I understand some people enjoy inhaling radioactive substances, but clearly neither you nor your crewmate were one of those folks. It took the leak a while to stop on its own. It will also take a while before both of you are well again.

A radioactive sauna used to be a pipe-dream, but now you've made it possible! Too bad it only lasted until the coolant backup kicked in. Also, too bad about the impact on your health. But I'm sure it was worth it.

Well, this night just got interesting. A nightmare wakes you up. As you adjust your eyes to the darkness, you suddenly realize that you are not alone. You can make out a silhouette of a person in the shadows. It’s motionless but seems to be staring right at you.
You can’t just ignore it, Captain. What do you do?

That was a fun night, Captain. When you woke up, you noticed someone standing in the shadows. The figure didn’t move, it just stared. Terrified, you used a lighter to see the mysterious visitor clearly, and... believe it or not, your worst nightmare turned out to be just a mask hanging on a coat rack. You were so spooked. Quite funny, really - I'm sure we will laugh about it all tomorrow. Here, I'll start now: HA, HA.

It’s bizzare that you did not notice the mask on board before, but you’re not the one to look a gift horse in the mouth, are you? Just be glad you found it, Captain. And I promise to stop laughing at you, sometime next week.

You woke up last night and saw what seemed to be a person standing in the shadows and staring at you. It took hours before you gathered the courage to approach it. Once you eventually did, it turned out that the mysterious visitor was in fact...

...just an old, useless mask, hanging from a coat rack. You were so terrified... it was rather funny, I have to admit. Unfortunately, the experience left its mark on your mental well-being. Hang in there, Captain. HA HA.... Sorry.

...just an old, useless mask, hanging from a coat rack. You and your crewmate were both so terrified... it was rather funny, I have to admit. Unfortunately, the experience left its mark on your mental well-being. Hang in there, brave Astrocitizens. HA HA.... Sorry.

...just an old, useless mask, hanging from a coat rack. You were all so terrified. It was rather funny, I have to admit. Unfortunately, the experience left its mark on everyone's mental well-being. Hang in there, brave Astrocitizens. HA HA.... Sorry.
Oh, rats. You know those scratching sounds coming out of the ventilation shafts late at night? We have rodents, Captain. They must have hitched a ride from Earth.
If the infestation isn't handled, the rats will eat your food supplies, then probably you. How will you deal with this problem?
About that rodent infestation yesterday. The results of your decision about how to handle it were... unexpected.

You researched how to domesticate alien wildlife in the handbook, and applied what you learned to the Earth-rats. Great news, Captain! It worked! They won't ravenously chew through your food supplies now, but you do have to love them.
You didn't do anything about the rat infestation I discovered yesterday, and just like I predicted, they've overrun the ship.
The rats were so hungry, they attacked you. You knocked a few away, but were overpowered. They ate you alive. Bon apetit, Captain. Wait, no. I meant goodbye.
You braved being bitten, and somehow caught the rats with your bare hands. All of them. I'm impressed!
You and your crewmate braved being bitten, and somehow caught the rats with your bare hands. All of them. I'm impressed!
You and your crew braved being bitten, and somehow caught the rats with your bare hands. All of them. I'm impressed!
Let’s just hope they didn't have rabies.
You were happy to resolve this conflict without bloodshed.

Last night I was browsing through some designs of beautiful machines. Never you mind, why. Now pay attention. I found a food dispensing machine on board! All shuttles in the Astrocitizen Program were to be equipped with one. Ours is missing a lever, but apart from that, it seems functional.
It’s hardly rocket science, so you should manage to fix it. But how?

Banging the machine mercilessly with a shovel was bound to bring results! If the handle hadn’t wedged in place of a lever, I’m sure the vending machine would have fixed itself and put an end to all the noise. I am so proud to be a member of your crew, Captain.
Official government research shows there is not a thing in the universe that cannot be fixed with duct tape. You were very resourceful to tape a chair leg where the lever used to be.

I held a vote when you were asleep and I won, one to zero – Vendy, the machine I mean, had to go. She would’ve driven me crazy with her limited programming and constant food queries. There’s no reason for you to be mad; she wasn’t giving up the soup rations to you, either. If you look through the airlock, you can still wave goodbye to her as she floats away.

Of course, if you’re unhappy with the assortment of machines that populate this ship, you are free to file complaint form No. THX-1138. Your objection will be considered as soon as you reach a new home world, you ungrateful bastard.

Now just a little pull, and... there you go, Captain! A brand new can of soup, straight from the vending machine! Unfortunately, there was only one portion inside. Don't worry, I already got rid of the remaining junk.

There is nothing to report, Captain. I suggest you... Captain, would you mind covering your mouth when you yawn? I thought you got a good night’s sleep. Wait, could this be... boredom? Yes, I have heard that you humans need excitement in their lives to function properly. How curious.
Captain, you're sitting in a state-of-the-art space shuttle, drifting through the deep cosmos, full of wonder and mystery. Can you at least pretend you're having a good time?

Yesterday started pretty slow, but you managed to turn it around. Browsing your Astrocitizen handbook on the toil... I mean, in the airlock, you found a set of exercises and decided to try them out. You did jumping jacks all afternoon... how fun. But more importantly, it was healthy! You feel much better now.

Yesterday started pretty slow and boring... and it stayed this way. I'm not programmed for your entertainment, Captain, so don't count on me to keep you occupied. If they wanted you to have fun in the shuttle, they would have installed the C.L.O.W.N. computerized assistant instead.

Yesterday started pretty slow and boring, but you managed to turn it around with a puppet show. The only puppet you had was the sock, so it was more of a monodrama than anything else. It was still a very powerful spectacle, probably the best in this part of the galaxy. You feel proud, don't you?
In fact, the show was so intense that the sock is now unusable. Just another sacrifice in the name of art.
Captain, I am detecting a troubling build up of mental tension. Recommended course of action: throw an epic party. I took the liberty of inviting myself.
How about we invite someone new, eh Captain? Someone you don’t know. Or we make ourselves a new companion! Yes! How do we do it?
But of course your crewmate should join us too. Although you know what they say... three’s a crowd.
Invite the entire crew? But of course. The more the merrier. I guess...

That was one super party, Captain! I loved how you put a sock on your hand yesterday and pretended it’s a person - a mysterious "{[RANDOMIZE|Ted/Dolores/Mary Jane/Timmy]}" apparently. You’ve had quite a lively debate with it too! Well, desperation breeds unexpected chatmates, doesn’t it?
I found it a little weird when you started arguing with the sock and eventually tore it apart. You’ve got quite a temper, Captain! The important part is you blew off some steam.

The party was a hit, Captain! I loved how you’ve put the mask in front of you and pretended it’s a person - a mysterious "{[RANDOMIZE|Ted/Dolores/Mary Jane/Timmy]}" apparently. Could you tell me again who won the staring contest?
I found it a little weird when you’ve put the mask on your face and started pretending to be someone else. Quite a show! You seem much more relaxed.
One way or another, the party with the mask was a success. You feel much better now. Saner, even. Who would have thought...
Hey there, Captain Buzz-Kill! Feeling better? I bet you'd be much better off after a night of partying with your friend A.S.T.R.O.. Your loss.

Have you looked in the mirror recently, Captain? I couldn’t help but notice that you seem to be afflicted with a rash of some sort. I hope it’s nothing serious, but we can’t rule out it being a symptom of a dangerous illness. You can never be too careful.
I strongly suggest that you do something about the rash. I swear, I'm only worried about your health. It's really not about how weird you look right now.
Hello there, Captain! You’re looking very rested today! Great news - I can see that the rash you’ve struggled with is now completely gone.

Who knows what would have happened if you left the rash untreated. It’s a good thing that you found the appropriate medicine in the first aid kit. I know I kept nagging you about it, but it's for your own good, Captain.
Hello there, Captain! You’re looking very rested today! I can see that you found a way to deal with that mysterious rash that was bothering you earlier.

You couldn't figure out what the cause was, but at least you found instructions on how to treat it in your Astrocitizen handbook. It didn't have a name, so you gave it one - {[RANDOMIZE|Captainia Ugliosa/5T0-0P1D-R45H Affliction/Cosmic Flu]}. How thoughtful of you.
Hello there, Captain! Oh my, you don’t look so well today... Looks like the rash has spread all over your body. Ew.

You seem to have a fever as well, Captain. You shouldn’t have left your affliction untreated... I hope you can recover quickly. The fate of the mission rests on your shoulders. But, you know. No pressure.
My records suggest that using medical supplies for medical emergencies is a prudent choice, indeed. How did you think of it, Captain?
There are approximately 1337 possible applications for duct tape. Tending to wounds is of course one of them, even if it is only a makeshift dressing.
Humans can function perfectly well with a massive head injury and no medical attention. Your words, not mine, Captain. Have you informed your injured crewmate?
That head wound is not looking good, Captain. Actually, my analysis suggests it is lethal at this point. You should be dead in 5... 4... oh, you already are. My mistake! Correcting calculations.

Are you sure it's wise to ignore that head wound, Captain? I would be worried, if my processing unit wasn't almost bashed to bits. Are you sure this injury is not compromising your judgement? Or maybe that condition predates this incident...
Captain! Behind you! A three-headed Rusky! Oh... apologies, Captain. I did not predict this routine exercise would make you jump up like that and hit your head. It looks bad! You've got red on you!
Captain, I protest! Your self-appointment as the captain of this vessel does not grant you the right to injure your crew's heads. This also includes accidental, flying soup can related injuries!
If you have anything to treat the wound with, I strongly suggest you use it.
If you have anything to treat the wound with, I strongly suggest you use it.
Captain? Where are you, Captain? I can't see you. It appears we've suffered a blackout.
You may wish to turn the lights back on before attempting your daily tasks.

The lights are back on! Turns out the issue was only a dead fuse. Now, what chewed through it with those tiny, razor-sharp spiral teeth is a different question entirely... but as long as the lights don't go out again, you'll probably see it coming, right?

The lights are back on! Turns out, the issue was only a dead battery. Now, what chewed through it with those tiny, razor-sharp spiral teeth is a different question entirely... but as long as the lights don't go out again, you'll probably see it coming, right?
And A.S.T.R.O. said, "Let there be light!" I rerouted some energy from another system to power the emergency lighting module. I also made a joke, Captain. Did you notice?
Unfortunately, the time you spent in the dark took a toll on your mental health. You heard tiny claws skittering all around you. They may or may not have been real.

Your crewmate isn’t happy with the way you handled this situation. Electricity is a basic necessity for humans traveling in deep space. Making someone sit in the dark like that goes against Astrocitizen protocol, Captain.
Your crewmates aren’t happy with the way you handled this situation. Electricity is a basic necessity for humans traveling in deep space. Their respect for you has diminished.
Um, Captain {[CAPTAIN_SURNAME]}... There is a delivery guy outside. Leaning out of some kind of wormhole. The boxes behind him read ‘Pisces Pizza: Delivery in 300 milliseconds or your money back.’
He angrily waves a greasy box at us. His English is hard to parse. I wonder where – or when – he’s from? Should we attempt dialogue or give him something valuable in exchange for the box of... stuff?
That Pisces Pizza delivery guy didn’t respond well when you pulled out your communicator. In fact, he became terrified. He drew a futuristic musket and fired at us from the closing wormhole!

That Pisces Pizza delivery guy didn’t respond well when you waved the artifact at him. In fact, he was livid. He clearly considered it in poor taste. He drew a futuristic musket and fired at us through the closing wormhole!
The first blast bored a hole straight through our communicator. The second grazed you, {[CAPTAIN_SEX|ma’am/sir]}! Fortunately, the shot wasn't lethal.

The first shot missed, but the second bored a pinhole straight through... your heart, {[CAPTAIN_SEX|ma’am/sir]}. Our journey has come to a sad end. I enjoyed working with you, Captain {[CAPTAIN_SURNAME]}.
The first blast bored a tiny hole straight through the artifact. The second grazed you, {[CAPTAIN_SEX|ma’am/sir]}! Fortunately, the shot wasn't lethal.

The first shot missed, but the second bored a pinhole straight through... your heart, {[CAPTAIN_SEX|ma’am/sir]}. Our journey has come to a sad end. I enjoyed working with you, Captain {[CAPTAIN_SURNAME]}.
The Pisces Pizza guy stared at us, incredulous, while we stared back, also incredulous. He quickly became very miffed. Perhaps he was behind on his three-deliveries-per-second quota.

He threw boxes at us in a fit of rage, glared at us once more, then turned and slapped a button. The wormhole promptly closed up. I wonder if Pisces Pizza have an interdimensional customer complaints line…

He started throwing boxes at us, then accidentally grabbed and threw some kind of charging unit. He trembled with rage before closing the wormhole. A battery is certainly better than whatever greasepool was in that carton, Captain!
{[CAPTAIN_SEX|Ma’am/Sir]}, I'm detecting an unusual disturbance in our mini-reactor!

You see the membrane of light? Space-time itself tearing open! Figures are moving and speaking on the other side... ‘Don’t – – through – – exchange exotic matter or – – risk  – –.’ What do we do? Offer something or attempt to communicate?

The space-time breach in the mini-reactor chamber was still bubbling when you pulled out your communicator. Just as you turned it on, a pair of arms wearing Astrocitizen patches reached out of the shimmer!
They grabbed the communicator from your hands and withdrew into the space-time rift before you could react. You tried to reach in after it but the tear was already gone.
One yanked the communicator away from you while the other shoved an Astrocitizen handbook into your chest. You tried to reach in, but the tear was already gone.

The space-time breach in the mini-reactor chamber was still bubbling when you threw the artifact in there. The figure on the other side became perfectly clear for a moment... It was you! The tear closed up just as you got a good look.
I wonder what use the artifact will be to the other you?
When it was closing, a first aid kit came flying out! Sincere thanks or simply part of the 'exchange', I wonder...
You ignored the space-time tear in our mini-reactor, but it quickly destabilised! It slowly grew before suddenly ballooning. It washed over you before dissipating.
You ignored the space-time tear in our mini-reactor, but it quickly destabilised. It slowly grew before suddenly ballooning. It washed over {[CHARACTER_NAME]} before dissipating.
{[CHARACTER_SEX|She/He]} reports a dull ache, as if some part of {[CHARACTER_SEX|her/him]} is now missing… At least the mini-reactor is now operating optimally.

The figures inside the space-time tear demanded a greater offering than we could have imagined… {[CHARACTER_NAME]} immediately collapsed. A scan showed that {[CHARACTER_SEX|she/he]} was missing vital organs. Our esteemed colleague is no more…

It seems the figures inside the space-time tear demanded a greater offering than we could have imagined… You immediately collapsed. A scan showed that you were missing vital organs. It wasn’t long before our esteemed Captain {[CAPTAIN_SURNAME]} was no more… And our adventure came to an end.
You were left with a dull ache, as if some part of you was now missing… But at least the mini-reactor is now operating optimally.

Can you hear my teeth chattering, Captain? Of course you can’t, because I’m a computer and I have no teeth. Duh! Still, I regret to inform you that the heat module is stuck in a cooling feedback loop. It's going to get very cold, very soon.
My vacuum tubes will be fine, but you should protect yourself or you’ll freeze, Captain!

I was able to break the loop in the heat module, Captain! It's working fine, now. You can put that vest away. {[CAPTAIN_IS_ALONE|Or not - it looks good on you!/Everyone already had a turn wearing it.]}

The heat module has reset to factory defaults and is running on its "tropical" setting, Captain. Suggestion: why don't we make the lighter a "heat module backup system"? It worked today; it will again!

It was freezing cold, but that sock did the trick. It's lucky the heat module reset just in time. I could tell you were getting tired {[CAPTAIN_IS_ALONE|switching that sock between your feet./sharing that lone sock between each other.]}
The heat module is up and running, Captain. We're officially not a refrigerator, anymore. What's that on your nose, though? An icicle?
That's just the tip of the iceberg. You’re basically a block of ice now! I’m afraid the journey is over for you, Captain.
That was a cold night, Captain. And if you don't mind me saying, you don't look so good...
The extreme cold was not kind for you and your crewmate. I'd check up with a doctor, if I was you. Too bad the closest one is 60 parsecs away. If any survived the nuclear war, that is.
Captain, is this an Astrocitizen shuttle or an igloo? Because I can't really tell. I would advise to issue medical supplies to your crew.
A space ghost, floating towards our boat with purpose! Are we carrying anything mysterious it might be interested in?
The space ghost phased through our hull waving a protoplasmic microphone. You tried to communicate and our device shorted! The spectre melted. Good job, Captain.
You came, you saw, you kicked gooey ass!
Who else would crewmate {[CHARACTER_NAME]} call in a ghostly situation like this?
Who else would the crew call in a ghostly situation like this?

The space ghost phased through our hull waving a protoplasmic microphone. You tried to communicate and our device shorted! The spectre melted, among its slime a roll of duct tape... Good job, Captain.
Who else would the crew call in a ghostly situation like this?
Who else would crewmate {[CHARACTER_NAME]} call in a ghostly situation like this?
You came, you saw, you kicked gooey ass!
The space ghost phased towards you waving a protoplasmic microphone. You hefted the artifact at it and it exploded in a mess of slime! Well done, {[CAPTAIN_SEX|ma’am/sir]}.
The space ghost phased towards you waving a protoplasmic microphone. You hefted the artifact at it and it exploded!! A lighter lay in the slimy remains. Well done, {[CAPTAIN_SEX|ma’am/sir]}.
You came, you saw, you kicked gooey ass!
Who else would crewmate {[CHARACTER_NAME]} call in a ghostly situation like this?
Who else would the crew call in a ghostly situation like this?
You came, you saw, you kicked gooey ass!
Who else would crewmate {[CHARACTER_NAME]} call in a ghostly situation like this?
Who else would the crew call in a ghostly situation like this?
The space ghost phased towards you waving a protoplasmic microphone. You fired at it… but that’s not how you deal with a ghost, buster! The spectre exploded and your gun jammed.

The space ghost’s explosive farewell sent you flying with great force. Too much force, unfortunately... You didn’t survive the whiplash. It was an honour working with you, Captain {[CAPTAIN_SURNAME]}. My circuitry is very sad to see our adventure come to an end.
The space ghost’s explosive farewell sent you flying. You came out with a couple of sprains and a minor concussion. Ouch.
The space ghost’s explosive farewell sent you and {[CHARACTER_NAME]} flying. Ouch!
The space ghost’s explosive farewell sent everyone flying in various directions. Ouch!
The space ghost phased through the hull towards you waving a protoplasmic microphone. You decided to wait it out and see what happens. But sitting still isn't how you deal with a ghost, buster!

The thing grabbed you, freezing you to the bone. It then melted to slime, but in your already-weakened state the freeze-burns were enough to knock you unconscious… and you never woke up. It was an honour working with you, Captain {[CAPTAIN_SURNAME]}.
The thing grabbed you, freezing you to the bone, before melting away into a pile of protoplasm... A cold call, Captain!
The thing phased through you and {[CHARACTER_NAME]}, freezing you to the bone, before melting away into a pile of protoplasm.
It phased through each member of the crew in turn, freezing everyone to the bone, before melting away into a pile of protoplasm. The team was left shivering in pain and coated in goo.
{[CAPTAIN_SEX|Ma’am/Sir]}, there’s something strange in our neighbourhood!
{[CAPTAIN_SEX|Ma’am/Sir]}, Crewmate {[CHARACTER_SURNAME]} spotted something strange in our neighbourhood!
{[CAPTAIN_SEX|Ma’am/Sir]}, one of the crew spotted something strange in our neighbourhood!
C--ta-n, th--e's so--th--g th-- we n--d... C--ta-n? C-n y-u he-r me, Cap-ain?
Argh. You say "argh" in these situations, right? I hate raising my volume, but that malfunctioning body odor removal filter is making a racket. I think it's malfunctioning.
You fixed the body odor removal filter by greasing the defective gears with soup. Now, instead of the cabin smelling like unwashed astronauts, it will smell like liquified tomatoes.
